summary: Master Power Purchase Agreements and Renewable Energy Contracts to structure bankable deals, negotiate risk clauses, and model revenue for sustainable investmen
lede: Power purchase agreement training helps energy and procurement professionals structure and negotiate renewable-energy contracts. Participants practice allocating generation, transmission and offtake risks, and modeling revenue under different pricing mechanisms. They also work on negotiating clauses such as curtailment and tariff escalation, and aligning PPAs with project financing and related agreements.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who must structure, negotiate, and finance bankable Power Purchase Agreements in competitive energy markets. Renewable Energy Project Manager:
audience: Structure bankable PPAs for solar and wind
Corporate Offtaker: Negotiate Virtual PPAs to meet
Energy Lawyer: Draft dispute resolution and change-in-law
Investment Analyst: Model revenue and calculate DSCR
Utility Procurement Officer: Align PPA terms
Sustainability Manager: Integrate PPA attributes into ESG
Financial Advisor: Synchronize PPAs with EPC, O&M
Hybrid Project Developer: Structure solar-plus-storage PPAs
Regulatory Analyst: Navigate policy impacts on PPA
Risk Manager: Identify and allocate curtailment
modules: Foundations of Renewable Energy Contracts and PPA Markets
Risk Identification and Allocation in Power Purchase Agreements
Financial Modeling and Bankability Analysis for PPAs
Negotiation Strategies and Contractual Clause Management
Specialized PPA Models for Storage and Hybrid Projects
ESG Reporting and Stakeholder Communication in Renewable Contracts
Integration, Strategy, and Executive Reporting for Renewable Contracts
Case Studies and Practical Lessons from PPA Transactions
Capstone: Complete Bankable PPA Framework Development
prerequisites: Prerequisites: Working knowledge of energy markets and intermediate Excel skills (pivot tables, basic formulas). No coding or advanced programming is required. Participants should bring a laptop for hands-on financial modeling exercises. A basic understanding of renewable energy technologies (solar, wind) is recommended but not mandatory, as foundational modules cover key concepts.
